label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
output:
**From: Amaka_Bio100 | 2026-11-08T22:16:00**

Tolu, good evening. I saw your message and I had to log in properly to reply, because I am literally you one year ago. I'm in Biology 100L right now, federal uni here in Lagos, and Medicine was what I put down. So let me answer your questions one by one, and I'll try to be honest with you instead of just telling you "accept it" or "rewrite."

First, the beginning, so you know I'm not talking from outside. Last year I scored 251 in JAMB, applied Medicine and Surgery, and they offered me Biology. The day I saw it on the portal, I locked myself inside my cousin's room in Surulere and cried. I didn't eat that day. My mum had already been telling people in church that her daughter is doing medicine — she did it for like two months before I could beg her to stop. So when you say you've been crying since afternoon, I understand it. It's not small thing. People who haven't been there will say "it's just admission" but they don't know.

Now to your real question: **can you actually transfer?** Yes. It is real. It is not a myth like Kingsley is saying. But it is also not as simple as favour is making it sound, and I want to be straight with you about that because I think that's what you're asking for.

What our level adviser told us — and this is my school, so please hear the last part of this message — is that to move to MBBS after 100L, you need a CGPA of at least 4.5 out of 5.0, *and* there must be space. Both. Not one. 4.5 is not a small thing. And "space" means they only take as many as the MBBS quota can carry. The adviser said last year about 6 people got moved in from the whole faculty. She thinks over 40 applied. So do the maths yourself. It happens — real people, real names — but it's 6 out of 40-something, not 40 out of 40.

She also said you need to meet the Medicine cut-offs for JAMB *and* post-UTME, not just the general school cut-off. This one is important for you specifically: 268 by itself doesn't establish that you're eligible. You scored 268 — that might meet your school's Medicine JAMB cut-off or it might not, depending on the school, and nobody here knows your post-UTME score. You have to check both. Go and find out your school's actual Medicine cut-off for JAMB and for post-UTME, and compare. If your post-UTME didn't clear it, the transfer conversation is different. Don't let anybody on this forum (including me) tell you yes or no without that information, because we don't have it.

And this is the part I really want you to take: **go to your faculty or department and ask for the exact transfer rules for your own school.** Write it down. Ask about the CGPA, ask whether it's 4.5 or something else, ask about the space, ask whether it's after 100L or after 200L, ask what happens to your JAMB and post-UTME scores. Every school runs this thing differently. What my adviser told me is my school's rule, not a national law. Forum people are useful for hearing experience, but we are not the authority. Even me — I'm telling you my experience, not your answer.

Now, how is it really, inside Biology 100L? The courses are BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. Honestly, the ones that deal with people are Physics and Maths. Those two are where people lose the CGPA they need. Biology and Chemistry most people can manage if they're serious. So if you're coming in with a transfer plan, know that Physics and Maths are the ones you have to respect from day one, not from exam week. My CGPA after first semester is 4.31, not 4.5, and I'm still trying. So I'm not sitting here as somebody who has made it. I'm somebody who is in it and still working.

Money side, so it doesn't surprise you: my lab coat was 6,500 naira, dissecting kit was 9,000, and the practical manual was extra on top. Small things, but they add up.

Is Biology bad as a course? No. I'll tell you the truth — I came in angry, and somewhere along the line something shifted. First BIO practical, we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted. I was fine. And that day I realised I actually like this thing. I'm enjoying genetics and cell biology more than I expected to. That is not me trying to make you feel better. It's just what happened. Biology is a real course with a future. It's just that it wasn't the course you wanted, and those are two different problems — the course being bad, and the course not being Medicine.

Which brings me to the question I think you should sit with before that acceptance fee deadline: **do you want Medicine, or do you want to be "doctor"?** Because those are not always the same thing, and sometimes the second one is really about your parents, or church, or what people will say. Nobody can answer that for you. But answer it honestly, because it changes everything. If it's Medicine itself, then transfer or rewrite both make sense and you pick based on your own capacity. If it's the title, then you might be about to waste years chasing something that won't satisfy you even if you get it.

Two stories for you on the rewrite side, since your aunty is pushing that. My secondary school classmate Ifeoma rejected a Pharmacy offer to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times. She is still at home. That's not me saying rewriting is bad — it's me saying the "one year is nothing" line that Kingsley gave you is only true if the one year actually ends in admission. Sometimes it doesn't, and then it's two years, then three. Staying at home is not as easy as people who have never done it like to say — favour is right about that part, you watch your mates move on and it weighs on you. But rewriting is also not wrong if you are genuinely ready to sit down and do the work again with your whole chest. If you know yourself and you know you'll read, it can work. If you know you'll be depressed and scattered at home, it probably won't.

So don't let anybody rush you into a decision with only half the information. Go and ask the department. Check your post-UTME against the Medicine cut-off. Find out the real CGPA and the real number of spaces in your school. Then look at yourself and decide whether you can chase 4.5 while doing Physics and Maths, or whether a rewrite is the cleaner road for you.

Whatever you choose, Tolu, it is not the end of the world. I know it feels like it is right now — I cried in Surulere, so I know. But one year from now you'll look back and see it was a bend in the road, not the end of it. Take care of yourself this week, eat something, and don't let the deadline pressure you into a decision you haven't thought through. If you want to ask me anything else, I'm here.
